title: Attention Mosaic Hint Engine: Hybrid kernel selection for mixed-length conversational loads
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build a lightweight hybrid heuristic (the Attention Mosaic Hint Engine) that chooses per-request attention/compute kernels and prefill/decode scheduling strategies for conversational workloads with mixed sequence length distributions. The engine balances tail-latency SLOs, per-token cost, and memory safety when serving heterogeneous GPUs and quantized kernels. It should be usable in hosted and dedicated modes with a low-risk rollout and a safe fallback to current default kernels.
acceptance_criteria: A1: For at least three benchmark conversational workloads (short-chat, mixed-turns, long-context synthesis), the hint engine reduces 95th percentile latency by >=10% vs current baseline without increasing token cost by >5%.
A2: The runtime exposes a per-request decision trace (kernel chosen, confidence, key features) recorded to telemetry for debugging and offline analysis.
A3: Safe fallbacks: if the probe or estimator is unavailable or reports low confidence, runtime falls back to existing stable kernel path and logs an incident metric.
A4: New autotune loop can run in canary (10% traffic) and be disabled via feature flag without server restarts.
A5: Documentation and a playbook for operations and rollbacks are published in Confluence.
A6: Unit/integration tests covering the probe, hint merge logic, and prefill->decode handoff are in CI and pass on CPU/GPU testbeds.
implementation_notes: Architecture: 1) Lightweight hardware fingerprint (occupancy, SMs, memory bandwidth estimates) computed at startup and periodically refreshed. 2) Sequence-length histogram sampler per-customer that keeps exponential moving average (EMA) of recent seqlen distribution. 3) Micro-prober modules: short synthetic kernels (microbenchmarks) executed warmstart-only during low-load intervals to estimate kernel throughput for given shapes. 4) Decision model: rule-based primary layer (heuristics derived from offline sweep) + fallback logistic regressor trained on offline microbenchmark dataset to compute confidence. 5) Two-phase decision: prefill stage picks kernel and whether to enable KV-prefix aggregation; decode stage may re-evaluate on first token decode using a low-latency probe to swap to a decode-optimized kernel (with KV migration path). 6) Safety: memory budget check and max-switch-rate limiter to avoid oscillation.
test_plan: TP1: Microbenchmark suite covering attention tile shapes (32x32, 64x64, 128x64 etc.) across NVidia A10/A100/RTX variants and quantized runtime path.
TP2: End-to-end latency/cost runs using conversational replay traces (prod-derived anonymized traces) for short/mixed/long workloads.
TP3: Chaos: inject delayed probe responses and simulate probe failures to validate fallbacks.
TP4: Memory overcommit scenarios to validate safe rejection and metrics emitted.
TP5: Regression tests ensuring identical outputs across kernel swaps within tolerances for numerical stability-sensitive models.
TP6: Canary rollout verification job that measures traffic split, SLOs, and automated rollback triggers.
rollout_notes: Phase 1: Internal testbeds + perf runs (complete). Phase 2: Canary (10%) on low-risk customers with monitoring and automatic rollback if regression detected. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Feature flagging per-customer and per-region must be available. Operator runbook: steps to disable hint engine, clear per-customer seqlen caches, and force single-kernel mode.
monitoring_metrics: m.hintengine.decision_rate: requests/sec with hint decision executed
m.latency.p50/p95 (by workload and by kernel path)
m.fallback.count: times fallback to baseline occurred
m.memory.oom_attempts when hint engine recommended high-mem kernel
